raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Adds an `SGLDCacheOptions` node that turns Cache-DiT on or off for a single run from the graph. It sets the options on a cloned MODEL, so toggling it never restarts the worker. The executor reads them from `transformer_options` and maps them to the per-request `enable_cache_dit` and `cache_dit_params`. The loader option stays as the fallback, and a per-run on/off wins over it.

Only MiniMax-H3 supports it. Other models send one independent step per request, so there is no step history to reuse, and the node rejects them with an error. TeaCache is not exposed because its state resets on timestep 0.

This is meant to line up with slimming `SGLDOptions` down to load-time options. If #43504 lands first I will rebase onto its `model_options` path.

Tested on CPU only (`test_comfyui_adapters.py`, `test_comfyui_generator.py`, 44 passed). GPU unit run is in the comments.

nodes.body:
GPU run on a Modal L4 (CUDA 13, torch 2.13 with the released sglang 0.5.21 deps, this branch's code on top, ComfyUI master checked out). Ran all `test_comfyui_*.py` plus `test_ipc_cuda.py`: 123 passed, 1 skipped, 3 xfailed. Plain main on the same box is 117 passed.

This does not exercise Cache-DiT on a real H3. The full H3 checkpoint is about 498 GB, so I did not run it. Treat the per-run on/off behavior as unit-tested only, and it would be good to have someone with H3 weights try it. The only skip is a test that needs a tiny H3 checkpoint.

Full details of the GPU run, so it can be reproduced.

**Environment**
- Modal, 1x NVIDIA L4 (sm_89)
- Image: `nvidia/cuda:13.0.1-devel-ubuntu22.04`, Python 3.11
- `pip install 'sglang[diffusion]'` (0.5.21) for the dependencies, which brought in torch 2.13. This branch is cloned and put first on `PYTHONPATH`, so the PR code is what runs.
- ComfyUI master cloned to `/comfy` and added to `PYTHONPATH`, so the tests that need `comfy` run instead of skipping.

**Command** (from `python/`)
```
PYTHONPATH=/comfy:. python -m pytest \
  sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_comfyui_*.py \
  sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_ipc_cuda.py -q -rfs
```
Baseline: plain `sgl-project/sglang` main on the same image gives 117 passed, 1 skipped, 3 xfailed.

**Result on this branch:** 123 passed, 1 skipped, 3 xfailed. The one skip needs a tiny H3 checkpoint.

**What this does and does not show**
- The rebased branch passes everything main passes, plus the Cache-DiT option tests, with ComfyUI installed and a CUDA device present.
- No failures were found on the GPU box for this branch.
- Cache-DiT itself was not run on a real H3. The full H3 checkpoint is about 498 GB, so I did not download it. The per-run on/off path is covered by unit tests with a fake executor, not by a real denoising run.
- Other models still reject the node by design, since they send one independent step per request.
Thanks! Can this be generic rather than H3-only? Also, please add an e2e run and share speed and quality numbers with it on vs off.

E2E numbers. H100, ComfyUI v0.39.2, Flux.1-dev, 1024x1024, 25 steps, euler/simple, cfg 1, same seed, default DBCache settings (Fn=1 Bn=0 W=4 R=0.24 MC=3). The worker log confirms one context for the whole run: `cache-dit enabled on transformer (steps=25, ...)`.

| | prompt time | PSNR | SSIM |
|---|---|---|---|
| native ComfyUI | 4.62s | | |
| SGLD cache off | 3.64s | 25.37 dB vs native | 0.903 vs native |
| SGLD cache on | 2.01s | 18.08 dB vs cache off | 0.616 vs cache off |

That is 1.81x vs cache off. With these defaults the output drifts noticeably (layout shifts a bit, still a clean image), so the default threshold is on the aggressive side for 25 step Flux. The node exposes the DBCache knobs for a more conservative setting.

![cache on vs off](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OnePunchMonk/sglang/304694ba10ce3c0fe70216f52eb475443d2d9188/43696_cache_on_off.png)

Follow-up with gentler DBCache settings, same H100 setup (Flux.1-dev, 1024x1024, 25 steps, same seed), compared against cache off:

- W8 R0.08: 1.37x, 22.5 dB PSNR / 0.81 SSIM
- W8 R0.12: 1.45x, 20.7 dB / 0.74
- W4 R0.12: 1.52x, 19.2 dB / 0.69
- Default W4 R0.24 (from above): 1.81x, 18.1 dB / 0.62

Every setting keeps a clean image, with the layout shifting more as the threshold goes up. To make sure the drift is Cache-DiT itself and not the per-run wiring, I checked that W25 (no caching possible) is bit-identical to cache off, and that a fresh mount and a later run with the same seed are bit-identical too.

The sweep also hit a crash when the knobs change between runs: cache-dit 1.5.1 leaves a class-level flag set after disable_cache on a bare transformer, so the remount asserted. Fixed in 7585fd52d9 with a regression test against the real cache-dit. This affects server requests that change cache_dit_params as well, not just ComfyUI.

![cache sweep](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OnePunchMonk/sglang/118b35e9f03052942228170190188f477ae4660e/43696_cache_sweep.png)

Hi @OnePunchMonk, I pushed one commit on top of your branch (814256ec76) so CFG > 1 runs are cached instead of rejected:

1. **Detect CFG from the guider**: the sampler wrapper checks `cfg != 1` and a `negative` cond, and the executor sends `comfyui_separate_cfg` (per-call `cond_or_uncond` is only `[0]` or `[1]`).
2. **Mount with separate CFG**: the worker treats the alternating cond / uncond requests as one step. Registered adapters (Z-Image / Qwen-Image / FLUX) ignore `has_separate_cfg`, so `enable_separate_cfg=True` is passed explicitly, for ComfyUI runs only.
3. **Results** (Z-Image Turbo, 30 steps, H200, warm): cfg 4: 6.5 s -> 4.1 s; cfg 1: 4.0 s -> 2.0 s. Switching cfg and cache on one worker remounts cleanly.
4. **Scope**: I dropped Cache-DiT from #44058 so this PR owns it; `enable_cache_dit` there stays the loader default you fall back to.

Feel free to rework or drop the commit.

Could you merge the latest main into this branch, resolve the conflicts, and update the docs and default parameter guidance? Please clarify the quality trade-off and consider a more conservative preset. I also reproduced an issue where switching to off/default after tuning the cache knobs raises a ValueError; users should be able to disable caching without resetting every knob.

@@ -177,3 +178,23 @@ Per sampler step:
 4. The worker pipeline is the native model class with modules trimmed to `transformer` + pass-through scheduler. A single-file checkpoint goes through `comfyui_checkpoints`. After the first step, conditioning stays in a worker session; later steps send latents and the timestep.
 
 Adding a model means a checkpoint spec plus a `ComfyUIModelAdapter`. There is no extra ComfyUI pipeline class.
+
+## Per-run cache options
+
+`SGLDiffusion Cache Options` takes a MODEL and returns a clone carrying a per-run Cache-DiT toggle (plus an optional preset and DBCache knobs; `-1` keeps the preset or server value). It is sent as a per-request sampling field, so changing it between runs does not restart the worker.
+
+- Works for every integrated-mode model. ComfyUI sends one request per DiT call, so the worker keeps one Cache-DiT context for the whole sampler run (sized from the run's `sample_sigmas`) instead of one per request.
+- CFG works: with `cfg` other than 1 and a negative prompt, the cond and uncond calls of a step count as one Cache-DiT step. A run that sends an uncond call while its guider does not run CFG raises a `ValueError`. MiniMax-H3 keeps its own run state and is not limited this way.
+- TeaCache is not exposed: H3 rejects `enable_teacache`, and the other models reset TeaCache state every request.
+- Quality trade-off: Cache-DiT reuses transformer residuals on steps where they barely changed, so the output is not bit-identical to the uncached run. It stays a clean image, but the layout shifts more as the threshold goes up. Measured on Flux.1-dev (1024x1024, 25 steps, euler, cfg 1, same seed, H100), against cache off:
+
+  | Setting | Speedup | PSNR | SSIM |
+  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+  | `conservative` preset (warmup 8, threshold 0.08) | 1.37x | 22.5 dB | 0.81 |
+  | warmup 8, threshold 0.12 | 1.45x | 20.7 dB | 0.74 |
+  | warmup 4, threshold 0.12 | 1.52x | 19.2 dB | 0.69 |
+  | server default (warmup 4, threshold 0.24) | 1.81x | 18.1 dB | 0.62 |
+
+  Start from `conservative` when the output should stay close to the uncached run, and raise the threshold for more speed. Explicit knobs override the preset.
+- `off` disables caching and ignores any knobs left set, so there is no need to reset them. `default` keeps the knobs and applies them only if the loader option or server enables caching.
+- `cache_mode` (and `cache_dit_tuning`) in `SGLDiffusion Options` sets the loader default. A per-run `on`/`off` wins over it; `default` falls back to it, and changing it does not restart the worker.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Per-run cache options carried in ``model_options["transformer_options"]``.
+
+They ride on a cloned MODEL, so changing them never touches the loader options
+and never restarts the worker.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Any
+
+CACHE_OPTIONS_KEY = "sgld_cache_options"
+
+# Measured on Flux.1-dev, 25 steps, 1024px, H100 vs cache off: 1.37x at
+# 22.5 dB PSNR / 0.81 SSIM; the server default (warmup 4, threshold 0.24) gives
+# 1.81x at 18.1 dB / 0.62.
+CONSERVATIVE_PRESET = {
+    "max_warmup_steps": 8,
+    "residual_diff_threshold": 0.08,
+}
+
+
+def build_cache_options(
+    enable_cache_dit: bool | None, cache_dit_params: dict[str, Any] | None
+) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Plain, pickle-safe options; unknown cache_dit_params keys raise.
+
+    Knobs are kept when caching is on or left to the loader/server default, and
+    dropped when it is off, so a tuned node can be switched off without resetting
+    every knob.
+    """
+    from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.cache.cache_dit_integration import (
+        resolve_cache_dit_request_overrides,
+    )
+
+    params = resolve_cache_dit_request_overrides(cache_dit_params)
+    # cache-dit asserts Fn >= 1 only once sampling has started
+    for knobs in (params, params.get("secondary") or {}):
+        fn = knobs.get("Fn_compute_blocks")
+        if fn is not None and fn < 1:
+            raise ValueError(f"Fn_compute_blocks must be >= 1, got {fn}")
+    if enable_cache_dit is False:
+        params = {}
+    return {"enable_cache_dit": enable_cache_dit, "cache_dit_params": params or None}
+
+
+def request_cache_dit_for_run(packed, transformer_options, separate_cfg: bool) -> None:
+    """Ask the worker to keep one Cache-DiT context for the whole sampler run.
+
+    ComfyUI sends one request per DiT call. With CFG the cond and uncond calls
+    alternate, which Cache-DiT counts as one step when mounted with separate CFG.
+    """
+    options = transformer_options or {}
+    if 1 in (options.get("cond_or_uncond") or ()) and not separate_cfg:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "Cache-DiT through ComfyUI got an uncond call in a run whose guider "
+            "does not run CFG; set cfg to 1 or turn Cache-DiT off for this run."
+        )
+    sigmas = options.get("sample_sigmas")
+    if sigmas is None or len(sigmas) < 2:
+        raise ValueError("Cache-DiT through ComfyUI needs the sampler's sample_sigmas")
+    packed.extra_req["comfyui_num_steps"] = len(sigmas) - 1
+    packed.extra_req["comfyui_separate_cfg"] = separate_cfg
+
+
+def guider_runs_cfg(guider) -> bool:
+    """Whether this sampler run evaluates cond and uncond every step.
+
+    ComfyUI skips the uncond branch at cfg == 1; guiders other than CFGGuider
+    (BasicGuider, custom ones) carry no cfg and run a single branch.
+    """
+    cfg = getattr(guider, "cfg", 1.0)
+    conds = getattr(guider, "conds", None) or {}
+    return cfg != 1.0 and "negative" in conds
+
+
+def with_cache_options(model, options: dict[str, Any]):
+    """Return a clone of ``model`` carrying ``options``; ``model`` is untouched."""
+    cloned = model.clone()
+    transformer_options = dict(cloned.model_options.get("transformer_options") or {})
+    transformer_options[CACHE_OPTIONS_KEY] = options
+    cloned.model_options["transformer_options"] = transformer_options
+    return cloned
+
+
+def read_cache_options(transformer_options: dict[str, Any] | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    return (transformer_options or {}).get(CACHE_OPTIONS_KEY) or {}

+class SGLDCacheOptions:
+    """Per-run Cache-DiT toggle on a cloned MODEL; never restarts the worker."""
+
+    @classmethod
+    def INPUT_TYPES(cls):
+        knob = {"default": -1, "min": -1, "step": 1}
+        return {
+            "required": {
+                "model": ("MODEL",),
+                "enable_cache_dit": (["default", "on", "off"], {"default": "default"}),
+            },
+            "optional": {
+                "preset": (["server default", "conservative"],),
+                "Fn_compute_blocks": ("INT", knob),
+                "Bn_compute_blocks": ("INT", knob),
+                "max_warmup_steps": ("INT", knob),
+                "max_continuous_cached_steps": ("INT", knob),
+                "residual_diff_threshold": (
+                    "FLOAT",
+                    {"default": -1.0, "min": -1.0, "step": 0.01},
+                ),
+            },
+        }

GPU run on a Modal L4 (CUDA 13, torch 2.13 with the released sglang 0.5.21 deps, this branch's code on top, ComfyUI master checked out). Ran all `test_comfyui_*.py` plus `test_ipc_cuda.py`: 123 passed, 1 skipped, 3 xfailed. Plain main on the same box is 117 passed.

This does not exercise Cache-DiT on a real H3. The full H3 checkpoint is about 498 GB, so I did not run it. Treat the per-run on/off behavior as unit-tested only, and it would be good to have someone with H3 weights try it. The only skip is a test that needs a tiny H3 checkpoint.

Full details of the GPU run, so it can be reproduced.

**Environment**
- Modal, 1x NVIDIA L4 (sm_89)
- Image: `nvidia/cuda:13.0.1-devel-ubuntu22.04`, Python 3.11
- `pip install 'sglang[diffusion]'` (0.5.21) for the dependencies, which brought in torch 2.13. This branch is cloned and put first on `PYTHONPATH`, so the PR code is what runs.
- ComfyUI master cloned to `/comfy` and added to `PYTHONPATH`, so the tests that need `comfy` run instead of skipping.

**Command** (from `python/`)
```
PYTHONPATH=/comfy:. python -m pytest \
  sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_comfyui_*.py \
  sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_ipc_cuda.py -q -rfs
```
Baseline: plain `sgl-project/sglang` main on the same image gives 117 passed, 1 skipped, 3 xfailed.

**Result on this branch:** 123 passed, 1 skipped, 3 xfailed. The one skip needs a tiny H3 checkpoint.

**What this does and does not show**
- The rebased branch passes everything main passes, plus the Cache-DiT option tests, with ComfyUI installed and a CUDA device present.
- No failures were found on the GPU box for this branch.
- Cache-DiT itself was not run on a real H3. The full H3 checkpoint is about 498 GB, so I did not download it. The per-run on/off path is covered by unit tests with a fake executor, not by a real denoising run.
- Other models still reject the node by design, since they send one independent step per request.
Thanks! Can this be generic rather than H3-only? Also, please add an e2e run and share speed and quality numbers with it on vs off.

E2E numbers. H100, ComfyUI v0.39.2, Flux.1-dev, 1024x1024, 25 steps, euler/simple, cfg 1, same seed, default DBCache settings (Fn=1 Bn=0 W=4 R=0.24 MC=3). The worker log confirms one context for the whole run: `cache-dit enabled on transformer (steps=25, ...)`.

| | prompt time | PSNR | SSIM |
|---|---|---|---|
| native ComfyUI | 4.62s | | |
| SGLD cache off | 3.64s | 25.37 dB vs native | 0.903 vs native |
| SGLD cache on | 2.01s | 18.08 dB vs cache off | 0.616 vs cache off |

That is 1.81x vs cache off. With these defaults the output drifts noticeably (layout shifts a bit, still a clean image), so the default threshold is on the aggressive side for 25 step Flux. The node exposes the DBCache knobs for a more conservative setting.

![cache on vs off](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OnePunchMonk/sglang/304694ba10ce3c0fe70216f52eb475443d2d9188/43696_cache_on_off.png)

Follow-up with gentler DBCache settings, same H100 setup (Flux.1-dev, 1024x1024, 25 steps, same seed), compared against cache off:

- W8 R0.08: 1.37x, 22.5 dB PSNR / 0.81 SSIM
- W8 R0.12: 1.45x, 20.7 dB / 0.74
- W4 R0.12: 1.52x, 19.2 dB / 0.69
- Default W4 R0.24 (from above): 1.81x, 18.1 dB / 0.62

Every setting keeps a clean image, with the layout shifting more as the threshold goes up. To make sure the drift is Cache-DiT itself and not the per-run wiring, I checked that W25 (no caching possible) is bit-identical to cache off, and that a fresh mount and a later run with the same seed are bit-identical too.

The sweep also hit a crash when the knobs change between runs: cache-dit 1.5.1 leaves a class-level flag set after disable_cache on a bare transformer, so the remount asserted. Fixed in 7585fd52d9 with a regression test against the real cache-dit. This affects server requests that change cache_dit_params as well, not just ComfyUI.

![cache sweep](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OnePunchMonk/sglang/118b35e9f03052942228170190188f477ae4660e/43696_cache_sweep.png)

Hi @OnePunchMonk, I pushed one commit on top of your branch (814256ec76) so CFG > 1 runs are cached instead of rejected:

1. **Detect CFG from the guider**: the sampler wrapper checks `cfg != 1` and a `negative` cond, and the executor sends `comfyui_separate_cfg` (per-call `cond_or_uncond` is only `[0]` or `[1]`).
2. **Mount with separate CFG**: the worker treats the alternating cond / uncond requests as one step. Registered adapters (Z-Image / Qwen-Image / FLUX) ignore `has_separate_cfg`, so `enable_separate_cfg=True` is passed explicitly, for ComfyUI runs only.
3. **Results** (Z-Image Turbo, 30 steps, H200, warm): cfg 4: 6.5 s -> 4.1 s; cfg 1: 4.0 s -> 2.0 s. Switching cfg and cache on one worker remounts cleanly.
4. **Scope**: I dropped Cache-DiT from #44058 so this PR owns it; `enable_cache_dit` there stays the loader default you fall back to.

Feel free to rework or drop the commit.

Could you merge the latest main into this branch, resolve the conflicts, and update the docs and default parameter guidance? Please clarify the quality trade-off and consider a more conservative preset. I also reproduced an issue where switching to off/default after tuning the cache knobs raises a ValueError; users should be able to disable caching without resetting every knob.
